transcript.content: Hello, and welcome. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi. Um... I guess what brings me in is that my body just feels totally out of my control lately. 

Like, a little while ago, I was just constantly moving—pacing around my apartment all night, making all these notes for a supper-club I was going to start. I just couldn't stop. But lately... I don't know, I'm just so slowed down. My sister is actually the one who pushed me to come in. She says it takes me forever just to get my shoes on now. Everything just feels really heavy and slow.
When you were pacing around at night and making all those notes for the supper club, how long did that period last?

Um... I'm not really sure exactly how many days it was. It's kind of a blur now. I just remember it went on for a while, where I just felt like I had to keep moving and planning. But I couldn't give you a specific number of days or anything like that.

Before this recent period where you were pacing and making all those notes, had you ever experienced other times in your life where you felt unusually energetic, needed very little sleep, or felt like your thoughts were racing for several days in a row?

No, I don't think so. I mean, I've had times where I felt pretty good or had a lot of energy, but nothing like that. That whole thing with the pacing and the notes... that was new. I've never really felt that out of control before.
Before that time when you were pacing around and making notes for the supper club, had you ever gone through a period of several weeks or longer where you felt very sad, hopeless, or depressed?

No, I don't... I don't think I've ever felt depressed like that before. I mean, I've had bad days, but never anything that lasted for weeks or where I felt completely hopeless. This heavy, slow feeling I have right now... it's really the first time I've ever experienced anything like it.
This heavy, slow feeling you're experiencing now—how long has that been going on?
It's been going on for a while now. I'd say... probably about three months. Yeah, this heavy, slowed-down part has been there for about three months.
When you were pacing around and making all those notes for the supper club, do you think that period lasted at least several days in a row—like maybe a week or more?

Yeah, it was at least a week. Maybe a little longer, honestly. I just remember it going on for days and days, where I was just constantly moving and writing things down. So, yeah, definitely a week or more.

During that week or more when you were pacing and writing notes for the supper club, did you feel like you needed much less sleep than usual—like you could get by on just a few hours and still feel rested and energized?

No, I don't... I don't really think so. I mean, I remember being really focused on writing everything down, but I didn't really notice anything different with my sleep. I definitely didn't feel like I could just get by on a few hours and still have energy, no.
During that week or more when you were pacing and writing notes, did you feel like you could accomplish anything or that your abilities were somehow enhanced compared to your normal self?

Yeah, I did. I mean, I honestly believed I was about to build the best bilingual supper club in the city. I felt like it was a sure thing, you know? I thought investors would be stupid not to back me... even though, looking back, I didn't actually have a job or any money lined up at all. But at the time, I just felt completely capable of pulling it off.
During that week or more when you were pacing and writing notes for the supper club, did you find yourself talking more than usual, or did people comment that you were talking a lot or very fast?

Yeah, definitely. I was talking so fast... to my sister, to some cooks I used to work with, even just random people at cafés. They'd try to cut in or say something, and I would just keep going. It was like... the words just had to come out, you know? I couldn't stop them even if I wanted to.

During that week or more when you were pacing around and making notes for the supper club, did the situation cause any serious problems in your life—like getting you fired from a job, damaging important relationships, or getting you into financial trouble? Or did anyone ever suggest you needed to go to the hospital?

Yeah, it definitely caused problems. I just... I haven't been able to hold together my work plans, or figure out my rent arrangements, or keep up with any family commitments. Everything just kind of fell apart. I couldn't even get basic responsibilities organized on my own anymore, so... my sister actually ended up taking me to the crisis clinic.
Besides this current heavy, slowed-down feeling that's been going on for three months, have you had other periods lasting at least two weeks where you felt sad, empty, or depressed?

Um, no, I don't think so. I mean, I've had bad days before, like anyone, but... nothing like this. This is really the first time I've felt this heavy and down for weeks on end. Before these last three months, I haven't really had any long periods where I felt depressed or empty.
